ABSTRACT  
Allenyl ketones are widely distributed in various bioactive molecules which lead their selective synthesis con -
tinues a hot research topic. Currently, most of the developed protocols require multistep and stoichiometric 
reactions together with noble metal catalysts. Herein, we developed a practical methodology to access allenyl 
ketones straightforwardly via multi-component coupling of 1,3-enynes, fluoroalkyl halides, arylboronic acids, 
and CO with nickel as the catalyst. A series of fluoroalkyl unit containing allenyl ketones were produced in 
moderate to good yields. This new procedure features cheap catalytic system, relatively mild reaction conditions, 
broad substrate scope, excellent regioselectivity, and attractive synthetic transformations of the obtained 
products.   
Allenyl ketones are potent structural units that are widely present in 
diverse natural products and biologically relevant molecules such as 
citroside A and ketosteroid isomerase inhibitor [ 1 ]. Furthermore, they 
are also versatile building blocks in synthetic chemistry to give further 
valued added chemicals [ 2 ]. Therefore, the selective synthesis of such 
unique frameworks has received considerable attention over the past 
decades. The conventional methods include ketonization of pre-formed 
allene precursors with aldehyde or carboxylic acid derivatives, the 
elimination of unsaturated ketones and Wittig reaction, etc. ( Fig. 1 b) 
[ 3 – 7 ]. Nevertheless, these approaches often require stoichiometric oxi -
dants and/or metal reagents and multi-step operations. In addition, 
some of the needed precursors are air/moisture sensitive and compli -
cated to prepare which further restrict the structure diversity of the 
products. In this context, the exploration of a general and practical 
alternative procedure to access allenyl ketones with readily available 
reagents is highly desirable. 
Multi-component reactions, due to the high step- and atom-economy, 
enables a rapid entry to build up molecular complexity from three or 
even more types of starting materials in a one-pot manner. By taking the 
advantages of carbon monoxide (abundant, readily available from 
carbon-containing wasters, etc.), carbonylative multicomponent reac -
tion offers ideal choice for the preparation of carbonylated compounds 
from readily available substates [ 8 ]. Without surprise, this type of 
strategy has also been explored in the synthesis of carbonyl-containing 
allenyl derivatives, such as palladium-catalyzed carbonylation of prop -
argyl alcohols or esters to produce 2,3-allenoic acid derivatives ( Fig. 1 c) 
[ 9 , 10 ]. Alcohols and amines were applied as the nucleophilic reagents in 
these reactions, however, for the using of carbon-based nucleophile as 
the coupling partner to produce alkenyl ketone product has not been 
achieved until the work from Guo and co-workers who recently reported 
a nickel-catalyzed four-component carbonylation of CF
3
-containing 1, 
3-enynes, arylboronic acids, and cyclobutanone oxime esters [ 11 ]. The 
reaction was performed under atmospheric pressure of CO and various 
tetra-substituted CF
3
-allenyl ketones were produced in good yields and 
selectivity. 
However, developing new carbonylation reaction to enrich the 
alkenyl ketone products based on inexpensive catalyst is still appealing.

component coupling of 1,3-enynes, fluoroalkyl halides, arylboronic 
acids, and CO to afford structurally diverse allenyl ketones ( Fig. 1 d) 
[ 12 ]. An array of valuable fluoroalkyl containing allenyl ketones were 
formed in good yields in general. This new methodology also features 
wide functional group tolerance, excellent regioselectivity, readily 
available raw materials, inexpensive nickel catalyst and relatively mild 
reaction conditions. 
To start the investigation, 1,3-enyne 1a (0.2 mmol), phenylboronic 
acid 2a (0.3 mmol) and perfluorobutyl iodide 3a (0.3 mmol) were used 
as the model substrates. A range of nickel precatalysts were firstly 
screened using 1,10-phenanthroline (phen) as the ligand in 1,4-dioxane 
at 70

another important factor for tuning the reaction outcomes, several bis- 
nitrogen ligands were tested ( L1 - L7 ). The utilization of phenyl- 
substituted phen ligand L2 resulted in an improvement in the yield of 
the desired product ( Table 1 , entry 9), while the bipyridine related li -
gands gave inferior results ( Table 1 , entries 10 – 14). To further increase 
the yield, the ratios of 1a / 2a / 3a and Na

It should be noted that, only fluoroalkyl-derived allenyl ketone 4a was 
exclusively obtained in all these reactions and no other regioisomers 
were observed. No desired product could be detected under higher 
pressure of CO while 1 bar of CO lead to decreased yield. 
Having established the optimal reaction conditions, we next turned 
our attention to explore the generality of this 1,4-fluoroalkylcarbonyla -
tion reaction. In the first stage, the scope with respect to various 1,3- 
enynes 1 with phenylboronic acid 2a and perfluorobutyl iodide 3a 
was examined ( Scheme 1 ). An array of aromatic groups at the 4-position 
or different alkyl groups at the 2-position of 1,3-enynes all worked well 
to generate the corresponding products ( 4a - 4p ) in moderate to good 
yields. Moreover, various functional groups on 1,3-alkynes were also 
well tolerated in this catalytic system, including halides ( 4c - 4e , 4h ), 
thiophene ( 4f) , methoxyl ( 4i ), ether ( 4k , 4j ) and pyridine ( 4k ). To our 
delight, 1,3-enynes with a trifluoromethyl group at the 2-position did 
not occur β -F elimination ( 4g - 4k ). When there was no substituent at the 
2-position, decreased yields were observed ( 4m - 4o ). This distinct 
reactivity may be due to the instability of the formed propargyl radical 
and the derived allenyl radical. Next, long chain octyl group and diverse 
heteroatom-substituted alkyl groups on the 4-position ( 4p - 4t ) of 1,3- 
enynes were applicable to this process as well. To demonstrate the 
versatility and practicality of this reaction, the model system was run on 
a 2.0 mmol scale under 5 bar of CO, achieving 76% yield of the desired 
product 4a . 
Subsequently, the scope of other coupling reagents, including aryl -
boronic acids and perfluoroalkyl halides were examined ( Scheme 2 ). 
Arylboronic acids bearing electron-donating groups (-Me, -Ph or – RO) at 
para- and ortho-positions could smoothly undergo the transformation to 
give the corresponding allenyl ketones ( 5a - 5f ) in 47 – 90% yields. The 
thioether ( 5g ) unit with coordinating ability was compatible with the

reaction as well. Electron-withdrawing acyl and ester groups were well 
suitable with the process ( 5i , 5j ), while aldehyde and cyano groups were 
sensitive to nucleophilic reagents and thus decreased yields were ob -
tained ( 5h , 5k ). Notably, halides such as F, Cl and Br were well tolerated 
and gave the desired products in moderate to good yields ( 5l - 5n ), which 
can offer the possibility for further derivatization via cross-coupling 
reactions. Moreover, naphthyl and heterocyclic boronic acids were 
also feasible in this reaction system ( 5o - 5q ). In the case of 4-vinylphenyl 
boronic acid, only 19% yield was attained, may be attributed that the 
double bond can have an effect on the radical addition step. Then, a 
range of perfluorinated and difluorinated halides, including sterically 
hindered and long chain iodides, participated in the reaction efficiently 
and the corresponding products ( 6a - 6e ) were afforded in moderate to 
high yields. Due to the increased bond energy, the reactions involving 
perfluorohexyl bromide and ethyl bromofluoroacetate ( 6f ) resulted in 
decreased yields. When trifluoroiodomethane was used as a precursor of 
⋅ CF
3 
radical, the expected product ( 6g ) was also furnished in 32% yield. 
To verify the synthetic potential of this nickel-catalyzed fluo -
roalkylcarbonylation reaction, additional efforts were directed towards 
Nazarov cyclization of the resulting allenyl ketones. A treatment of 
phenyl allenyl ketone 5a with DMSO at 160 
◦
C led to the formation of 
cyclized product 7a in 63% yield with good stereoselectivity ( Scheme 3 ). 
Furan- and methoxyl-substituted allenyl ketones were applicable to this 
intramolecular cyclization as well. However, it is worth noting that in 
the case of electron-withdrawing cyanide-derived allenyl ketone 5k , 
domino cyclization and isomerization of carbon-carbon double bond 
executed, giving rise to indanone 7c as the main product. To probe the 
reaction mechanism, radical inhibition experiments were carried out. 
The yield of 4a gradually decreased with increasing the dosage of radical 
scavenger 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidinooxy (TEMPO, 0 – 3 equiv) 
( Scheme 3 , bottom). This result reveals that radical intermediates may 
be involved in this 1,4-fluoroalkylcarbonylation of enynes. 
In conclusion, we have developed a practical multi-component 
coupling of 1,3-enynes, fluoroalkyl halides, arylboronic acids, and CO 
enabled by nickel catalysis.
15 
This fluorocarbonylation process enables a 
rapid assembly of structurally diverse fluoroalkyl-derived allenyl ke -
tones. This protocol features inexpensive catalytic system, mild reaction 
conditions, good functional group tolerance, and excellent regiose -
lectivity. More importantly, the resulting products can also undergo 
intramolecular cyclization to furnish a variety of indanones.
